story_summary: Test Login functionality for the dashboard
functional_intent: Validate that users can authenticate using their registered email and password, receive appropriate feedback, and be redirected to the dashboard while ensuring security controls such as brute‑force protection are enforced.
in_scope_features: Error message display for invalid credentials
Brute‑force protection (account lockout after configurable failed attempts)
user_flows: Successful login: enter valid email and password → click login → credentials validated → redirect to dashboard
Invalid credentials: enter valid email with wrong password → click login → error message displayed
Invalid email format: enter malformed email → click login → client‑side validation error
Empty password: enter email, leave password blank → click login → client‑side validation error
Brute‑force lockout: exceed max failed attempts → account locked → subsequent login attempts show lockout message

risk_areas.description: Potential for credential stuffing or brute‑force attacks if lockout logic is bypassed.
Incorrect handling of edge cases such as empty fields or special characters in email.
Password must never be logged or transmitted in plain text.
Unclear or missing error messages can lead to user confusion.
Login response time must remain within acceptable limits under load.

acceptance_criteria_breakdown.description: Users must be redirected to the Dashboard upon successful login.
testable_points: Valid email and password are accepted.

acceptance_criteria_breakdown.description: Passwords must be masked during entry.
testable_points: Password field input type is password.
Characters are hidden (e.g., bullets) as user types.

acceptance_criteria_breakdown.description: An error message must appear for invalid credentials.
testable_points: Incorrect password with valid email triggers error.
Error message is visible, descriptive, and follows UI guidelines.
Error does not expose whether email or password was wrong.

acceptance_criteria_breakdown.description: The system must prevent "Brute Force" attacks.
testable_points: After configurable number of consecutive failed attempts, account is locked.
Locked account returns appropriate lockout message.
Lockout duration or reset mechanism follows security policy.

test_design_notes: Focus on both client‑side and server‑side validation. Include cross‑platform checks (Web, Android, iOS) for UI elements such as password masking. Verify that no sensitive data appears in logs or network traces. Consider load testing the authentication endpoint to ensure performance targets. Ensure error messages are generic to avoid user enumeration. Validate that lockout counters reset after successful login or after defined timeout.
